newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish banks PBI, Prosper sales seen at year-end.
newsitem.headline: Polish banks PBI, Prosper sales seen at year-end.

text.p: Poland's central bank plans to sell a majority stake in Polish Investment Bank SA (PBI) and Prosper Bank SA to a strategic investor around the turn of the year, PBI's president said on Thursday.

"(The stakes) should be sold around the end of the year...and I definitely think they will be sold by the end of the first quarter of next year," Lech Kurklinski told reporters after a news conference.

Kurklinski said both foreign and domestic investors were interested in buying shares from the central bank, the National Bank of Poland (NBP) in PBI and Prosper Bank, in which the NBP holds 100-percent and 93-percent stakes respectively.
At the news conference Kurklinski said the European rating agency ICBA had initiated coverage of PBI with a BBB- long-term rating, a B short-term rating, a C individual rating and a 2 legal rating.
"It shows we're an attractive bank in an attractive country," Kurklinski said, referring to ICBA's latest BBB long-term rating and A3 short-term rating for Poland.

Kurklinski also said PBI had made an 85.1-million-zloty pre-tax profit over the first three quarters of 1996 and expected to make a pre-tax profit of 100 million zlotys this year and a net profit of more than 60 million.
Last year PBI had a net profit of 26.2 million zlotys.
Kurklinsk said the NBP would retain a stake in PBI, with another minority stake going to employees.
He said a capital rise was likely some time next year and that a detailed plan would be available once the strategic investor was secured.
